FAILED WRITER-SAMPLE REPRODUCTION. All 1,493 posted recipients reproduce both published rating-weighted means and the repeated-measures F test at printed precision (main PDF p. 8). After exact matching with whitespace removed, all 250 included Experiment 3 writers (125 AI, 125 Google) have ratings. However, the recipient file contains 126 unique AI texts and 127 unique Google texts, versus 125 per arm stated on main PDF p. 8. Three additional advice texts cannot be linked to any included writer and account for 11 AI and 25 Google ratings. It cannot be established from these files that these are three additional independent randomized writers or that they should be included after the reported writer exclusions. They are not silently counted as people. Restricting to the verified writer sample leaves 1482 AI ratings and 1468 Google ratings, with respective means 3.556005398111 and 3.814032697548; these do not jointly reproduce the printed means. The reported rating analysis therefore cannot be reproduced on the confirmed writer sample. In accordance with the reproduce-first rule, no participant SD, effect, or SE is computed and all computed fields are null. The paired recipient test above is a reproduction diagnostic, not an eligible paired AI-assistance design: writer assignment is between people. No first-round writer result is appropriate.

All 2,402 posted rows across three arms; the file matches the final sample after five unrelated-advice exclusions and 98 technical exclusions (supplement PDF p. 2). No additional exclusions or missing-value drops. Outcome column: wordcount; treatment condition=gpt, control condition=google. Each data row is one writer with one advice output; the posted numeric score is used directly, without rerunning spaCy or substituting a different tokenizer. Sample SDs use n - 1. Difference is treatment minus control in the original outcome units. SE is from OLS of the writer outcome on an intercept and treatment indicator with HC2 covariance. No standardized effect or sign reversal is applied. The conventional ANOVA checks reproduce the printed test only; that ANOVA is not used for the new SE. The study_n_analyzed and omnibus checks cover all three arms, not the two-arm contrast; only the named two arms enter the computed HC2 result. Google has 787 people, plain GPT has 803, and GPT-links has 812. All pairwise contrasts share their corresponding original arm samples. Printed means have two decimal places (supplement PDF p. 5).

FAILED REPRODUCTION. SA2_data.csv has 1999 complete data rows (975 ChatGPT, 1024 Google), whereas supplement PDF p. 6 states 1976 analyzed people. No attention-check or exclusion flag is supplied. On all posted rows num_unique_entities averages 2.915897435897 (ChatGPT; rounds to 2.92, printed 2.91) and 2.834960937500 (Google; printed 2.83). The F statistic and p-value round to the printed values, but the available-data residual df is 1997, not the printed 1971. Neither the sample nor both arm means reproduce; no post-hoc exclusions, truncation of the treatment mean, SDs, or effects are supplied. All computed fields are null, including se_type because no SE was estimated.

skipped.reason: Set-level diversity has no independent participant outcome. The saved cosine_similarity column averages to 0.158829141649 in treatment and 0.057471178201 in control, with 547 and 557 posted writers. The paper uses separate condition-specific LDA models followed by PCA, not a named neural embedding model (main PDF p. 4). The trained models, topic counts, preprocessing, fitting seeds, and PCA settings or topic vectors are not supplied in the deposit. Averaging precomputed scalar scores does not reproduce that procedure from the same texts. Skipped under rule 5; the saved scores are not treated as independent participant values for SDs or HC2.

Set-level diversity has no independent participant outcome. The saved edit_distance column averages to 481.588839559415 in treatment and 531.856347600180 in control, with 547 and 557 posted writers. The paper states average pairwise Levenshtein distance, but does not supply its exact text preprocessing or pairwise inputs. Exact character-level Levenshtein distance on the deposited advice does not recover even the first saved row average within either arm (treatment: raw 599.538461538462, saved 589.509157500000; control: raw 562.937050359712, saved 557.755395700000). Thus the saved scalar scores cannot establish an exact reproduction of the set measure from the same processed texts. Skipped under rule 5; no participant SD or SE is constructed from these mutually dependent row averages.
